A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same information-flow study. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original token-masking experiments, information-flow measurements, classifier evaluation, and item-negligence analyses across several text-to-image models.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds mitigation comparisons, classifier experiments, user-controlled disambiguation, and closed-model evaluation.

M1.justification: The core masking and representation-patching procedures remain unchanged. v3 replaces the default k-NN redundancy classifier with a single linear layer and extends patching to accept a user-specified word meaning in Appendix G. These are bounded adaptations of the existing framework.

E1.justification: DrawBench, PartiPrompts, and the 110-prompt leakage set remain in use. Appendix G adds generated ambiguous prompts evaluated against user-selected meanings, extending the task beyond recovering an unambiguous intended interpretation. The added Nano-Banana evaluation uses the existing leakage prompts.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 introduces RAG-Diffusion as an evaluated mitigation baseline for both FLUX variants. Appendix D also compares logistic regression and the retained k-NN method against the new default linear classifier; v2 reported only k-NN classifier performance. These additions substantially expand direct comparative evaluation.

E3.justification: New experimental protocols include user-specified sense matching in Appendix G and an image-only, paired-context leakage test for Nano-Banana in Appendix H. Classifier comparisons introduce balanced, L2-regularized logistic regression and a linear layer trained for 25 epochs with binary cross-entropy. The existing main benchmark setup and 80/20 classifier split are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a pretraining co-occurrence analysis, user-controlled polysemy experiments, mitigation of the existing runway gender-bias example, and closed-model word-order sensitivity analysis. The item-negligence investigation is retained in Appendix F, including its 88% omission finding and 67%/33% diagnostic breakdown.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five images generated with different random seeds per main benchmark prompt and retain the same annotation-agreement statistics. v3 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practices.

E6.justification: v3 adds initial/RAG-Diffusion/patching leakage rates of 79%/39%/20% for FLUX-dev and 94%/43%/14% for FLUX-schnell, new classifier scores, 95% user-selected-sense success, and Nano-Banana leakage rates of 26% overall and 42% when the cue precedes the item. The 93% finding changes from patched-image correction in v2 to contextualized-versus-cleaned item diagnosis in v3, preventing a direct performance comparison. The former 31% syntactically unrelated-flow result disappears; Figure 3 and Table 1's original accuracies remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The patching equation, token-subset formulation, and formal influence criterion retain their meaning. Neither version provides theorems or proofs, and v3's conceptual clarifications do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims of concentrated token representations and occasional cross-item leakage remain. v3 foregrounds efficient image-free token identification in the Introduction and presents pruning and patching as demonstrated practical contributions in the Abstract and Conclusion, modestly extending v2's emphasis on diagnosis and promising interventions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes legitimate contextual interpretation from leakage in unambiguous cases and removes v2's assertion that these failures cannot be mitigated during image generation. It adds interpretations involving user control, bias mitigation, and generalization to closed models, while acknowledging that closed-model representations cannot be inspected or patched. The original Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds classifier training details, specifies three human annotators, describes human screening for unambiguous leakage prompts, and replaces the anonymous prompt repository reference with a named project repository. However, it removes the explicit 6,966-token classifier sample count and the appendix's PartiPrompts count, category exclusions, and license disclosure.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantive connections to SuperBPE, Wang et al.'s mechanistic spatial-relation work, Zarei et al.'s text-embedding study, and Ventura et al.'s complementary diffusion-side leakage mitigation. It also adds the mitigation-baseline citation and removes references associated with the former MrT5/ByT5 discussion. The overall positioning around encoder-level causal interpretation remains.

P1.justification: The Abstract, Introduction, methodology explanation, and Discussion are extensively revised. Experimental Setup becomes a separate section, redundancy prediction moves into the main text, negligence moves to Appendix F, Discussion precedes Related Work, and the appendices are reorganized into A–H. These substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces its runway panel with a pool-context comparison; the runway example becomes an expanded mitigation Figure 7. v3 adds the polysemy-control Figure 13 and mitigation Table 4, expands classifier displays into Tables 2 and 5, adds relative reductions to Table 1, and relocates the negligence figure to the appendix.

improvement.justification: The mitigation baseline in Table 4, classifier tradeoffs in Table 5, and clearer distinction between leakage and legitimate ambiguity make v3's recommendations better supported and easier to assess. The gains remain limited: unchanged Table 1 does not establish the new classifier's end-to-end alignment benefit, Appendix G omits the sample count behind its 95% result, and Appendix H infers encoder mechanisms from images alone. Some reproducibility details are also lost.
